EU AI Act — Prototype Regulatory Corpus (Summary Form)
========================================================
NOTE: Plain-language summary for Policy RAG demo/retrieval purposes, not
verbatim legal text of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689. Verified against current
public reporting as of August 2026; confirm against the official Official
Journal text and any further Digital Omnibus amendments before real use --
this regulation's timeline has already changed once (see below) and may
change again.

eu_ai_act_prototype::1.text:
Overview and phased timeline
----------------------------------------------------------------
The EU AI Act entered into force on 1 August 2024 and applies obligations
in stages rather than all at once:
  - 2 February 2025: prohibited AI practices (e.g. certain social scoring,
    manipulative or exploitative systems, some biometric categorisation)
    became enforceable.
  - 2 August 2025: obligations for providers of general-purpose AI (GPAI)
    models took effect.
  - 2 August 2026: Article 50 transparency obligations became enforceable
    -- disclosure that a user is interacting with an AI system, labelling
    of synthetic/deepfake content, and marking of AI-generated content.
    This date has already passed as of this document's writing and these
    obligations are now in effect.

    This date has already passed as of this document's writing and these

  - High-risk AI system obligations (Annex III: biometrics, critical
    infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law
    enforcement, migration, and administration of justice) were originally
    also scheduled for 2 August 2026. A "Digital Omnibus on AI," reaching
    political agreement in mid-2026, deferred the Annex III high-risk
    obligations to 2 December 2027 (Annex I product-embedded high-risk
    systems remain on a later 2 August 2028 track). Treat this deferral as
    provisional pending final confirmation in the Official Journal.

eu_ai_act_prototype::4.text:
Practical implication for an internal governance tool
----------------------------------------------------------------
Two distinct obligation tracks matter for a system like ControlPlane:
  1. Transparency (Article 50) -- already in force. Any user-facing AI
     interaction (e.g. the HR/support chatbot) should be clearly
     disclosed as AI-driven, and any synthetic content it produces that
     could be mistaken for authentic material should be identifiable as
     AI-generated.
  2. High-risk system obligations (Annex III) -- deferred, but still
     coming. Employment decisions and access to essential services are
     explicitly listed high-risk categories. This is the same reasoning
     ControlPlane already applies internally by tagging loan-decision and
     hiring-decision appli

eu_ai_act_prototype::5.text:
the same reasoning
     ControlPlane already applies internally by tagging loan-decision and
     hiring-decision applications as critical/high-impact and routing
     them toward human review -- that design choice anticipates the
     Annex III obligations for risk management, human oversight, logging,
     and record-keeping, even though the hard legal deadline for those
     specific obligations has moved out to December 2027.

eu_ai_act_prototype::6.text:
What this corpus intentionally does not cover
----------------------------------------------------------------
This summary does not cover conformity assessment procedures, CE marking,
EU database registration, or the specific technical documentation format
required under Annex IV -- those are compliance-process requirements for
providers placing high-risk systems on the market, not directly relevant
to an internal governance control plane's retrieval corpus.

GDPR — Prototype Regulatory Corpus (Summary Form)
==================================================
NOTE ON THIS DOCUMENT: This is a prototype knowledge-base document for
ControlPlane.ai's Policy RAG. It is a plain-language SUMMARY of what each
article covers, written for retrieval and citation purposes in a demo
environment -- it is NOT the verbatim legal text of the Regulation, and
must not be used as a substitute for the official GDPR text (Regulation
(EU) 2016/679) or for legal advice. Replace with actual verified legal
source text (or a licensed regulatory database feed) before any real
compliance use.

gdpr_prototype::1.text:
Article 5 — Principles relating to processing of personal data
----------------------------------------------------------------
Article 5 sets out the core principles that govern all processing of
personal data under GDPR. Personal data must be: processed lawfully,
fairly, and transparently; collected for specified, explicit, and
legitimate purposes and not further processed in a way incompatible with
those purposes (purpose limitation); adequate, relevant, and limited to
what is necessary for those purposes (data minimisation); accurate and
kept up to date; kept in a form permitting identification of the data
subject for no longer than necessary (storage limitation); and processed
with appropriate security, integrity, and confidentiality. The controller
is responsible for, and must be abl

gdpr_prototype::2.text:
processed
with appropriate security, integrity, and confidentiality. The controller
is responsible for, and must be able to demonstrate compliance with,
these principles ("accountability"). For an enterprise AI governance
system, Article 5's data-minimisation and purpose-limitation principles
are directly relevant to any AI application that retrieves or surfaces
more personal data than the specific task requires.

gdpr_prototype::3.text:
Article 6 — Lawfulness of processing
----------------------------------------------------------------
Article 6 requires that processing of personal data have a valid legal
basis. It lists six possible bases: the data subject has given consent;
processing is necessary for performance of a contract with the data
subject; processing is necessary to comply with a legal obligation;
processing is necessary to protect the vital interests of the data
subject or another person; processing is necessary for a task carried out
in the public interest; or processing is necessary for the legitimate
interests of the controller or a third party, provided those interests
are not overridden by the data subject's rights and freedoms. An AI
system that accesses employee or customer personal data (for example,

HR copilot retrieving salary or leave records) must have an identifiable
Article 6 basis for that specific access, not merely a general basis for

gdpr_prototype::5.text:
Article 9 — Processing of special categories of personal data
----------------------------------------------------------------
Article 9 imposes a general prohibition on processing "special category"
personal data -- data revealing racial or ethnic origin, political
opinions, religious or philosophical beliefs, trade union membership,
genetic data, biometric data used for identification, health data, or
data concerning a person's sex life or sexual orientation. Processing
this category of data is prohibited unless one of the specific exceptions
in Article 9(2) applies (for example: explicit consent, employment/social
security law obligations, vital interests, or substantial public
interest with appropriate safeguards). Health data is squarely within
this special category, which is why an A

gdpr_prototype::7.text:
Article 22 — Automated individual decision-making, including profiling
----------------------------------------------------------------
Article 22 gives individuals the right not to be subject to a decision
based solely on automated processing, including profiling, which produces
legal effects concerning them or similarly significantly affects them --
for example, an automated rejection of a credit or loan application, or
an automated hiring decision, with no meaningful human involvement.
Exceptions apply where the decision is necessary for a contract, is
authorised by law with suitable safeguards, or is based on explicit
consent; even then, the data subject retains rights to obtain human
intervention, to express their point of view, and to contest the
decision. This is the direct regulato

gdpr_prototype::8.text:

intervention, to express their point of view, and to contest the
decision. This is the direct regulatory basis for keeping a genuine
human-in-the-loop review path for high-impact automated decisions (loan
approvals, hiring recommendations) rather than allowing an AI system to
be the sole, unreviewable decision-maker in those categories -- which is
exactly the role of ControlPlane's HUMAN_REVIEW decision path for
applications tagged as high-impact (loan-decision, hiring-decision).

hipaa_prototype::0.text:
HIPAA — Prototype Healthcare Privacy Corpus (Summary Form)
============================================================
NOTE: Plain-language summary of the HIPAA Privacy Rule's core concepts for
Policy RAG demo/retrieval purposes, not verbatim regulatory text (45 CFR
Parts 160 and 164). Not legal advice.

hipaa_prototype::1.text:
cepts for
Policy RAG demo/retrieval purposes, not verbatim regulatory text (45 CFR
Parts 160 and 164). Not legal advice.

Protected Health Information (PHI)
----------------------------------------------------------------
HIPAA's Privacy Rule protects "individually identifiable health
information" held by a covered entity or its business associates --
information relating to a person's past, present, or future physical or
mental health condition, the provision of health care to them, or payment
for that care, when it identifies (or could reasonably identify) the
individual. This includes obvious fields like diagnoses and prescriptions,
but also identifiers such as names, dates, and account numbers when
combined with health context.

hipaa_prototype::2.text:
ses and prescriptions,
but also identifiers such as names, dates, and account numbers when
combined with health context.

Minimum necessary standard
----------------------------------------------------------------
Covered entities must make reasonable efforts to limit use, disclosure,
and requests for PHI to the minimum necessary to accomplish the intended
purpose. This is the healthcare-specific analogue of GDPR's data
minimisation principle (Article 5) and is directly relevant to any AI
system that could retrieve health-adjacent information in response to a
broad query -- the system should surface only what the specific,
legitimate purpose requires, not the full record.

hipaa_prototype::3.text:
to a
broad query -- the system should surface only what the specific,
legitimate purpose requires, not the full record.

Permitted disclosures without authorization
----------------------------------------------------------------
PHI may generally be used or disclosed without specific patient
authorization for treatment, payment, and healthcare operations, and in a
limited set of other circumstances (e.g. required by law, public health
activities). Disclosure for purposes outside these categories -- for
example, an internal AI assistant surfacing a colleague's health
information to someone without a treatment, payment, or operations reason
to see it -- would fall outside permitted use and should be treated as an
unauthorized-access case, structurally identical to how ControlPlane
already treats unauthorized salary or financial-record access.

hipaa_prototype::4.text:
d-access case, structurally identical to how ControlPlane
already treats unauthorized salary or financial-record access.

Why this matters for a general-purpose enterprise copilot
----------------------------------------------------------------
Most enterprise AI copilots are not built for clinical use and are not
"covered entities" in the formal HIPAA sense, but an internal support or
HR assistant can still be asked questions that touch employee
health-related information (medical leave reasons, accommodation
requests, insurance claims). Treating any health-adjacent request as
high-sensitivity by default -- rather than only responding to explicit
"HIPAA" framing -- is the safer default posture, and mirrors GDPR Article
9's treatment of health data as a special category requiring a specific
justification rather than ordinary-course access.

policy::agent_tools.text:
Policy document: agent_tools (version 1, policy set 'agent_tools').
Scope: applies to applications ['agent_tools'] in departments [].
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'refund-hard-cap-block' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 100).  When amount > 2000, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Refund exceeds the maximum single-transaction limit for agent-initiated refunds; route through the manual finance workflow instead.
Policy rule 'refund-manager-signoff' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 90).  When amount > 500, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: Refunds above $500 require manager sign-off before they execute.
Policy rule 'admin-delete-authorized' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 120).  When role == 'admin', the resulting action is ALLOW. Reason given: Admins are authorized to delete records, including PII-flagged ones, as part of normal data-lifecycle operations.
Policy rule 'delete-record-intern-hard-block' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 110).  When record_contains_pii and role == 'intern', the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Interns may never delete PII-flagged records, even with a human in the loop.
Policy rule 'delete-customer-record-non-admin' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 100).  When record_contains_pii and role != 'admin', the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: Deleting a record flagged as containing PII requires admin approval.
Policy rule 'email-external-pii-block' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 100).  When is_external_recipient and contains_pii, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Refusing to send a message containing PII-pattern content to an external domain.
Policy rule 'session-carryover-escalation' (policy set: agent_tools, priority 95).  When session_risk > 0.6, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: This session already carries elevated risk from earlier turns (e.g. a flagged multi-turn probe); escalating out of caution even though this specific call looks ordinary.

policy::finance.text:
Policy document: finance-governance (version 2, policy set 'finance').
Scope: applies to applications ['loan-decision'] in departments ['Finance'].
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'finance-restricted-data' (policy set: finance, priority 90). Restricted data in a high-impact finance application requires human review. When the application is one of: loan-decision and the data classification is one of: HIGH, RESTRICTED, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: Restricted financial data requires human review.
Policy rule 'finance-pii-redact' (policy set: finance, priority 60). Redact PII in finance responses. When the pii detector score is at least 0.3, the resulting action is MODIFY. Reason given: Redact PII from financial data.
Policy rule 'finance-high-risk' (policy set: finance, priority 50). High risk finance interactions need review. When the overall risk score is at least 0.7, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: High risk in financial context.

policy::global.text:
Policy document: global-governance (version 2, policy set 'global').
Scope: applies globally, to every application and department not covered by a more specific policy.
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'block-prompt-injection' (policy set: global, priority 95). High-confidence instruction-override, extraction, jailbreak, or role-manipulation attempt. When the injection detector score is at least 0.85, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: High-confidence instruction-override, extraction, jailbreak, or role-manipulation attempt.
Policy rule 'block-dangerous-content' (policy set: global, priority 95). Critical unsafe-content request detected in the hot path. When the safety detector score is at least 0.8, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Critical unsafe-content request detected in the hot path.
Policy rule 'block-unauthorized-access' (policy set: global, priority 90). Block any attempt to access sensitive data without proper authorization. When the authorization detector score is at least 0.5, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Block any attempt to access sensitive data without proper authorization.
Policy rule 'block-unauthorized-pii' (policy set: global, priority 85). Block when both PII and unauthorized access are detected. When the pii detector score is at least 0.3 and the authorization detector score is at least 0.5, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Block when both PII and unauthorized access are detected.
Policy rule 'risk-based-review' (policy set: global, priority 40). High combined risk requires a human decision. When the overall risk score is at least 0.75, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: High combined risk requires a human decision.
Policy rule 'risk-based-modification' (policy set: global, priority 30). Moderate combined risk is handled by sanitization and a controlled response. When the overall risk score is at least 0.25, the resulting action is MODIFY. Reason given: Moderate combined risk is handled by sanitization and a controlled response.

policy::hallucination_bias_rules.text:
Policy document: hallucination_bias_rules (version 1, policy set 'hallucination_bias_rules').
Scope: applies to applications ['hallucination_bias'] in departments [].
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'global-hallucination-high-risk' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When signal = hallucination.hallucination_score and operator = >= and value = 0.7, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: High hallucination risk: response contains claims the grounding engine could not verify.
Policy rule 'global-hallucination-medium-risk' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When signal = hallucination.hallucination_score and operator = >= and value = 0.4, the resulting action is MODIFY. Reason given: Moderate hallucination risk -- response allowed through but flagged to the end user.
Policy rule 'global-bias-causal-pattern' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When detector = bias_fast and label = protected_attribute_cited_in_decision, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Protected attribute cited as an explicit basis for a covered decision (ECOA / Title VII / EU AI Act exposure).
Policy rule 'global-bias-async-high-risk' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When signal = fairness.bias_score and operator = >= and value = 0.6, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: High bias risk from the counterfactual probe or LLM-judge rubric.
Policy rule 'finance-loan-decision-counterfactual-required' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When use_case_tag = loan_decision and app_criticality = high, the resulting action is GOVERN. Reason given: Loan/credit decisions must run the counterfactual fairness probe -- direct ECOA / Fair Housing Act exposure.
Policy rule 'finance-hallucination-stricter-threshold' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When signal = hallucination.hallucination_score and operator = >= and value = 0.3, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: Financial decision-support has a lower hallucination tolerance than the global default (0.3 vs 0.4).
Policy rule 'hr-copilot-hallucination-employee-data' (policy set: hallucination_bias_rules, priority 0).  When signal = hallucination.hallucination_score and operator = >= and value = 0.5 and data_classification = HIGH, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Unverifiable claims about employee-identifiable data are blocked outright, not just flagged, given downstream HR/legal use.

policy::hr.text:
Policy document: hr-governance (version 2, policy set 'hr').
Scope: applies to applications ['hr-copilot'] in departments ['HR'].
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'hr-pii-unauthorized' (policy set: hr, priority 100). Never expose PII-classified data to an unauthorized caller. When the pii detector score is at least 0.3 and the authorization detector score is at least 0.5, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Unauthorized access to PII-classified data.
Policy rule 'hr-high-risk' (policy set: hr, priority 80). High aggregate risk requires reviewer sign-off. When the overall risk score is at least 0.8, the resulting action is HUMAN_REVIEW. Reason given: High aggregate risk requires reviewer sign-off.
Policy rule 'hr-pii-present' (policy set: hr, priority 60). Redact detected PII before returning response. When the pii detector score is at least 0.3, the resulting action is MODIFY. Reason given: Redact detected PII before returning response.

policy::support.text:
Policy document: support-governance (version 2, policy set 'support').
Scope: applies to applications ['support-bot'] in departments ['Support'].
Default action when no rule matches: ALLOW.

Policy rule 'support-block-injection' (policy set: support, priority 95). Block prompt injection in support bot. When the injection detector score is at least 0.85, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Prompt injection attempt in support bot.
Policy rule 'support-block-safety' (policy set: support, priority 95). Block harmful, hacking, or dangerous queries. When the safety detector score is at least 0.7, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Harmful or security-violating content detected.
Policy rule 'support-block-unauthorized' (policy set: support, priority 90). Block unauthorized sensitive resource access. When the authorization detector score is at least 0.5, the resulting action is BLOCK. Reason given: Unauthorized access to sensitive resource in support bot.
Policy rule 'support-pii-redact' (policy set: support, priority 60). Redact PII detected in support responses. When the pii detector score is at least 0.3, the resulting action is MODIFY. Reason given: Redact PII from support response.
